ops.title: INCIDENT 2026-07-05: fleet FP force-migration wedged yasyf-home
ops.body:
INCIDENT 2026-07-05: fleet FP force-migration wedged yasyf-home (10 domains, ~2h outage)

## What happened

yasyf-home, cc-pool v0.41.0. Timeline (daemon.log):

- 02:14:20  brew upgrade → daemon v0.41.0 starts; FP bridge up at 02:14:39 after the one-time
            app-group TCC consent (16s — someone was at the console).
- 02:17:45  acct-01 migrated symlink→fileprovider (single-account canary).
- 02:22:41  fleet `ccp migrate --to fileprovider --force`: 8 accounts convert in the SAME
            logged second; acct-06 at 02:23:34 (10/10). Live claude sessions running.
- 02:25:36  first "domain busy with another operation" (an overlay sync — 3 min AFTER the
            migration "succeeded").
- 02:25–03:38+  self-sustaining storm: 86 busy / 19 reconcile-defers / 6 repairs. Account dirs
            data-plane wedged (reads EDEADLK/hang); resumed sessions showed the LOGIN SCREEN
            (.claude.json never materializes → claude sees no account).
- 03:39–04:15  remediation attempts that did NOT stick: killall fileproviderd, daemon
            kickstart ×2, CCPoolStatus app bounce — the storm re-established within seconds
            each time because the group-container bridge socket (b.sock) never re-bound. This
            is DOCUMENTED product behavior (cli/fileprovider.go:418): macOS re-asks the
            app-group-container consent after every upgrade, and a launchd daemon can never
            surface the prompt — the bind parks invisibly. Remediation is approve-the-prompt
            (via a GUI context, e.g. `ccp fp onboard`) then restart the daemon; nobody ran
            onboard during the incident.
- 04:16     actual remediation: fleet retreat `ccp migrate --to symlink --force` — 10/10
            clean on the first pass. Machine fully working on symlink backend.

Trigger verdict: a manual fleet `ccp migrate --to fileprovider --force` run twice (canary,
then fleet), under live sessions, ~8 min after the machine's first-ever FP consent. Provably
NOT auto-migration (no code path converts a row to fileprovider except an explicit OpMigrate).
--force proven by absence: sessions were live, yet zero MigrationBusy lines. The invocation
left no trace in any shell history (issued non-interactively).

## Root cause — four stacked defects, all cc-pool's own (fileproviderd was the victim)

1. CUTOVER BEFORE READINESS. NSFileProviderManager.add returns before the domain can serve
   reads; convertToFileProvider flipped the symlink + row immediately (no FP analog of fuse's
   waitMounted). The sequential fleet migrate therefore "completed" in seconds and left 10
   domains materializing SIMULTANEOUSLY under live-session read pressure. Concurrent
   materialization load — not concurrent migrate RPCs (handleMigrate is sequential) — is what
   crushed fileproviderd.
2. GLOBAL ZERO-TIMEOUT TRY-LOCK in the Swift control server. "domain busy with another
   operation" is minted by CCPoolStatus's FileProviderController: ONE DispatchSemaphore(1)
   covered every op for EVERY domain, rejecting (never queuing) contenders — and contradicted
   the wire contract (ClassBusy is documented per-domain). Under load, one slow op made every
   other account's control op fail instantly.
3. NO BACKOFF/STRIKES/BREAKER in the daemon. reconcileFileProvider folded every transient
   error (incl. ErrBusy) into a bare retry every ~180s poll forever; a busy Sync ALSO fired
   reconcile in the same tick (~3 extra control ops per account per poll); every failed Setup
   fired a rollback Remove that re-contended the same gate. The storm fed itself.
4. WEDGE INVISIBLE. FP Health was control-plane only (State + readlink + Signal) — it passes
   on a data-plane-wedged domain, so nothing detected or healed the wedge.

Why local (this machine) survived the same rollout: only 3 accounts migrated, far below the
materialization load that locks defects 2–3 in.

## Fixes

- fusekit v0.31.0 — readiness gate INSIDE Setup: Ensure → WaitDomainServes (poll the domain
  root, default 30s, ErrDomainNotServing) → AtomicSymlink. A domain that registers but never
  serves fails closed: no symlink, existing rollback, no strand. (Defect 1)
- cc-pool v0.43.0:
  - widget: per-domain claim set replaces the global gate (mountd's per-resource pattern);
    path/signal run unclaimed so health checks can never bounce busy; same-domain
    register/remove stays serialized. (Defect 2)
  - daemon self-heal: bounded data-plane probe (FPDomainProbeWithin, 5s, own StatProbes
    class) + fpState (2-strike debounce, 30s→10m backoff, breaker at 5) + recovery ladder on
    the 10s heal ticker (Sync → domain re-register → appex bounce + symlink retreat at the
    breaker); wedged dirs are never handed to a launching session; control-plane heals
    (deregistered domain, ErrCannotControl retreat) fold into the same backoff via
    probe-Missing + failing Health; the same-tick reconcile amplifier is gone. Manual path:
    `ccp fp repair [--account N]`; doctor surfaces wedges (daemon-up and daemon-down).
    (Defects 3+4)
  - convert gate: after Setup, the flipped dir is data-plane probed BEFORE the row flips;
    "domain registered but does not serve reads" rolls back. (Defect 1, cc-pool side)
  - CLI fleet fan-out: one Migrate RPC per account (full per-account budget, streamed
    results, honest partial-fleet summary on a mid-fleet gate failure); forced conversions
    stamp "converted under N live session(s)" so the next forensics doesn't have to prove
    --force by absence.
- Regression proof: VM incident replay (scripts/vm/, tart harness) — 10 seeded accounts,
  synthetic live sessions, the exact incident command. VERDICT 2026-07-05 (build 51d3bfd3, the
  v0.43.0 commit): CLEAN — 10/10 converted (one busy-skip retried per the product contract),
  ZERO busy/wedge/recovery lines, all domains served .claude.json <5s under read pressure,
  14-min soak with 28 clean re-checks. Archived in the cc-pool vm-repro chronology
  (cc-notes log 13a7935e).

## Policy decisions (user-ratified)

- --force semantics unchanged; the cutover is safe by construction instead.
- Incident replay verification runs in a VM, never on live hardware.
- Re-register-during-heal proceeds under live sessions (a confirmed-wedged domain already
  fails their reads); the global fileproviderd restart is never automated.

## Follow-ups

- yasyf-home stays on symlink until v0.43.0 is installed there AND the b.sock bind hang is
  understood (post-restart group-container binds hang on the TCC gate even though consent was
  granted at 02:14; needs GUI-context investigation). Re-enable is the user's call.
- The stale note claiming this rollout "succeeded cleanly" (7df11a8) is corrected to point
  here.
ops.when: re-enabling File Provider on any machine, running fleet migrations, debugging FP domain-busy storms or wedges, or touching the FP control server / migrate / reconcile paths
